transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I, um... I guess I'm here because, well, even when I'm feeling a bit better, I just... I can't quite shake this feeling. It's probably nothing, and I feel a little silly even bringing it up, but... I just feel like some of the people at my church, and in my walking club, are... watching me? And sometimes I think they might be putting little messages about me in the church bulletin, or, you know, just in the things they say when I'm around. Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I hope that's the kind of thing you wanted to know.

Can you tell me more about the feeling that people are watching you and sending messages about you? For example, do you believe they are intentionally trying to communicate something specific to you through their actions or words?

Well, like I was just saying, it's just this lingering feeling. I really hate to even say it out loud because I don't want to speak ill of anyone—they are lovely people, really! But... yes, sometimes it does feel intentional. Like they're hinting at things about me. 

I'll read a little phrase in the Sunday bulletin, or hear a comment someone makes while we're walking, and it just feels so... pointed? Like they're trying to let me know they're keeping an eye on me, or that they know things about my life. Even on my good days when I'm feeling perfectly fine otherwise, I just can't quite shake it. I try to just smile and be polite because I really don't want to make a fuss or cause any trouble. 

Am I explaining that okay? I know it probably sounds a bit ridiculous to a professional like you, and I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of nothing.
Have you ever felt certain, even without clear proof, that these messages or observations about you are part of a coordinated effort, or do you mostly just suspect it could be the case sometimes?

Oh, well... I certainly wouldn't want to accuse anyone of coordinating anything. That sounds so... so serious, doesn't it? I'm sure they're all very nice people, and I'd hate to think they were plotting against me or anything like that. 

It's more just... well, like I mentioned, I just can't quite shake the feeling that they're watching me, and that those little messages in the bulletin or the things they say are about me. Even on my better days, when I'm feeling quite cheerful, that feeling just sort of... lingers. I mostly just suspect it, I suppose. I don't have any real proof, and I'd never want to cause a scene by asking them about it. 

I hope that answers your question? I'm trying my best to explain it properly, but I know I probably sound a bit silly.
Have you ever felt that these messages or comments were revealing personal information about you that others shouldn't know, even though there’s no clear evidence that they actually do?

Oh, um... well... I wouldn't say they're revealing deep, dark secrets or anything like that. I really don't want to make it sound like they're being malicious. They're good people. 

But... yes, I suppose sometimes it does feel like the little things they say, or those little notes in the bulletin, are touching on things about my life that... well, that I haven't told them. Just small things, you know? But it's enough to make me feel like they're keeping tabs on me somehow. And like I said before, it's just this feeling I can't shake, even when I'm having a good day and feeling fine otherwise. I just feel like they're watching me and slipping those little messages in. 

I know I don't have any proof, and I'd never confront anyone about it because I'd hate to be a bother. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information. I really don't want to seem like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill.
Have you ever changed your behavior, avoided certain places or people, or taken any specific actions because of these feelings that others are watching you or sending you messages?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say I've made any drastic changes. I still live at home, of course, and I try to keep things as normal as possible. I really don't want to be an inconvenience to anyone. 

But I suppose... well, I have stopped going to my quilting gatherings and the walking club. And I haven't been keeping up with my gardening as much as I used to. It's just... sometimes it feels a bit easier to stay home where it's quiet, you know? Just to avoid those uncomfortable feelings. 

And, well, my daughter is so sweet, she's started checking in on me a bit more often—making sure I'm eating my meals and getting to my appointments. I feel terrible that she has to take time out of her busy day for me, but she insists. 

I hope that's not too unusual? I just thought it was best to take a little step back from things, but I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart. Am I doing okay explaining all this?
Have you ever felt completely certain about these messages or being watched, even when others might say there’s no reason to believe it?

Oh, dear... "completely certain" sounds so... so stubborn of me, doesn't it? I really wouldn't want to argue with anyone if they told me I was mistaken, and I'd hate for you to think I'm being difficult. 

But... well, I suppose that's actually the main reason I came in to see someone in the first place. It's just that... even on my better days, when my mood is perfectly fine and I'm trying my best to be positive, I just can't seem to shake the feeling. It's mostly some of the people at church, and from the walking club... I just can't help but feel they're watching me. And that they're putting those little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin, or hiding them in the things they say when we chat. 

I know others might say there's no reason to believe it, and I really don't want to sound unreasonable or ungrateful for the people in my community... but the feeling is just so persistent, no matter how hard I try to brush it off. 

I hope I'm explaining that right? I really want to be helpful, and I hope I'm answering your questions the way I'm supposed to.

Have you ever believed, without any actual proof, that something strange or unusual was happening involving you and others, even though it seemed completely plausible to you and fit with how you saw the world at the time?

Oh, well... I suppose that's very similar to what we were just talking about, isn't it? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I'd hate to waste your time. 

But yes, that's really the whole reason I'm here. It's just... even when I'm feeling perfectly fine, like on a really good day when my mood is up, I just have this... this belief, I guess you could call it. It's those folks at church and the walking club. I just feel so certain that they're keeping an eye on me, and slipping those little messages about my life into the Sunday bulletin or into our casual conversations. 

It feels completely real to me, even though I know I don't have any hard proof to show you or anyone else. I really don't want to sound like a foolish old woman making up stories. I know they're lovely people, and I feel awful even thinking these things... but the feeling just doesn't go away. 

Does that answer what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Even though you say you don't have proof, do you feel deep down that your belief about being watched and receiving hidden messages is absolutely true, no matter what anyone else might say?

Oh, dear... well... yes, I suppose I do. I feel just terrible admitting it because I know how it must sound to you, and I really don't want to come across as stubborn or unreasonable. 

But yes, even when my mood is perfectly fine and I'm having a lovely day... I just feel it so deeply. It's the main reason I came in, really. I just can't seem to shake the feeling that those folks at church and the walking club are watching me, and leaving those little messages about me in the bulletin and in the things they say. 

I know it might sound silly to someone else, and I'd never want to argue with anyone about it... but deep down, it just feels so absolutely true to me. I'm so sorry if that's not the right way to think about things. Am I making any sense at all? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining it to you.
Can you think of a time when someone said or did something that seemed completely normal to you at first, but later you realized it was actually about you or connected to what you were thinking?

Oh, my... well, I feel terrible because I feel like I'm just giving you the exact same answer again. I really hope you aren't getting frustrated with me, I know I must sound like a broken record. 

But yes, that happens quite a bit, actually. At first, someone from the walking club will just say something casually, like... oh, maybe they'll mention something about keeping a tidy house, or there will be a little innocent-looking reminder in the church bulletin about being a good neighbor. It seems completely normal when I first hear it or read it. 

But then... well, later on, I'll be sitting at home, and it just clicks. I'll realize they were actually talking about *me*. That they've been watching me, and they deliberately slipped those little messages into what they were saying, or printed them in the bulletin, just for me to find. 

And like I mentioned before, this happens even on my better days, when my mood is perfectly fine and I'm feeling quite cheerful. It's really the whole reason I finally decided to come in and see you, because I just can't shake the feeling that they're doing it, no matter how hard I try to ignore it. 

I know it sounds a bit strange when I say it out loud, and I feel so silly admitting it... Did I explain that okay? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right kinds of examples.
